name: Cotton Candy
lede: Cotton candy is the pale sugar pink of the fairground sweet, and a crayon name that has become a color word.

sections.title: A pink named for a sweet
sections.body:
St. Clair's glossary of color names defines sugar as a sweetish pink, the color of cotton candy [1]. The name works as a plain comparison: the color is what the confection looks like. Our library also lists it as a Crayola color, though the year is not in our data [2].

On screen it is a light, bright pink close to [[baby-pink]], with [[carnation]] as a deeper neighbor. Compared with plain [[pink]], it leans slightly toward violet, the direction of [[mauve]]. The word itself has a modern curve: in printed English it peaks in the 2010s and rose fastest in the 2000s, though the phrase also names the sweet, so the curve is not the color alone [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only one painting in our archive of 23,781 holds this color, as photographed [3].
